overview: The day was dominated by Alexei Starovoitov's major 21-patch series (v2) to remove hard-coded limits on maps, kfuncs, subprograms, and special fields in BPF programs, enabling arbitrarily large and complex BPF programs. Mike Bazov submitted two separate series addressing preemption safety in tracing programs, fixing per-CPU private stack usage and raw tracepoint regs slot lifetimes. Additional patches addressed TCP ECN per-connection callbacks, mprog RCU synchronization performance, libbpf BTF enum sign-extension fixes, and selftest portability improvements on non-x86 hardware.

patches.title: bpf: Remove the limits on maps, BTFs and fd_array of a program
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: Part of a sweeping 21-patch series (v2) that removes all hard-coded BPF program complexity limits. This patch specifically lifts the caps on the number of maps, BTF objects, and fd_array entries a single program can reference. The motivation is to allow real-world programs—especially those generated by compilers or frameworks—to grow beyond the arbitrary limits that have historically constrained them. Companion patches in the series remove BPF_MAX_SUBPROGS, lift kfunc table size limits, and optimize the verifier's dominator algorithm to O(n log n) to remain tractable at larger scales.

patches.title: bpf: Remove BPF_MAX_SUBPROGS
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: Removes the BPF_MAX_SUBPROGS constant (historically 256) that capped the number of subprograms in a single BPF program. This unblocks large programs that use many helper functions or rely heavily on tail calls and subprogram dispatch. The change is part of the broader limit-removal series and is paired with refactoring the call graph representation to use edge lists instead of fixed arrays, which keeps memory usage proportional to actual program complexity.

patches.title: bpf: Find dominators in O(n log n)
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: Replaces the verifier's dominator-tree computation with an O(n log n) algorithm (Lengauer-Tarjan) to remain tractable as program sizes grow beyond the now-lifted hard limits. The previous algorithm had worst-case quadratic behavior that became a bottleneck for large programs. This is a correctness-neutral performance improvement that makes the rest of the limit-removal series viable without introducing unacceptable verification latency.

patches.title: bpf: Avoid per-CPU private stack in preemptible tracing progs
patches.author: Mike Bazov
patches.summary: First patch in a 4-patch series (v3) that fixes a class of data corruption bugs in preemptible BPF tracing programs. Per-CPU private stacks are unsafe when a tracing program can be preempted and re-entered on the same CPU; this patch switches such programs away from per-CPU storage to avoid the overlap. The series also introduces a new mechanism to check and enforce per-task recursion limits via bpf_ctx, replacing the coarser per-CPU recursion guard for programs that can be preempted.

patches.title: bpf: Disable preemption while a raw tracepoint regs slot is in use
patches.author: Mike Bazov
patches.summary: A standalone fix that prevents a race condition where a raw tracepoint's regs slot could be overwritten if the BPF program running on it is preempted and another program runs on the same CPU and also uses a raw tracepoint. The fix disables preemption for the duration of the regs slot's use, which is a minimal and targeted intervention. This addresses a subtle correctness issue in multi-program tracing setups on preemptible kernels.

patches.title: bpf: tcp: add ecn_init callback to bpf_tcp_ops for per-connection ECN
patches.author: Irlanki Sandeep
patches.summary: Adds an ecn_init callback to the bpf_tcp_ops struct, allowing BPF programs to override ECN (Explicit Congestion Notification) initialization on a per-connection basis. This is v9 of the patch, indicating a long review cycle with significant iteration. The feature enables network operators to implement custom ECN policies in BPF without modifying kernel code, complementing existing BPF hooks for congestion control.

patches.title: bpf, mprog: Defer RCU synchronization until peer reuse
patches.author: Qi Wu
patches.summary: Optimizes the multi-program (mprog) framework by deferring expensive RCU synchronization calls until a peer slot is actually reused, rather than synchronizing on every detach. Unnecessary RCU synchronizations add latency to program detach operations, which is noticeable in environments that dynamically attach and detach BPF programs frequently. This v3 patch improves operational efficiency for high-churn mprog use cases such as tc and XDP program management.

patches.title: libbpf: Fix sign extension of unaligned enums in btf_dump_get_enum_value()
patches.author: Hungyu Lin
patches.summary: Fixes a libbpf bug where enums with sizes smaller than 4 bytes (unaligned enums) would have their sign extension computed incorrectly when dumping BTF data. This caused negative enum values to be printed as large positive numbers, breaking BTF-based introspection tools. The fix is part of a 2-patch series (v3) that also adds a selftest to verify correct dumping of unaligned enums and zeroed fs_context structures.
